HUNT: partial. All five fixes were hunted and probed against commit 18b5a15 (the PR head on origin). Two gaps:
- (a) Something else rewrote the worktree's history while I was working. At 11:11:23 it ran `git reset --soft HEAD~1`, then recreated the history as b240eec (tests) and 155c32a (fix). I did not cause this: none of my commands mutate anything, and `src/` has no `git reset` call. To avoid reviewing a moving target, I re-ran the suite and all probes against a `git archive 18b5a15` copy in a temp dir. I did not diff 155c32a against 18b5a15, so if the recreated commits differ in content, I haven't reviewed them.
- (b) I did not probe a bare-repo main worktree for `primaryCheckoutRoot`. In that layout `worktrees[0]` is the bare dir, so `worktreeRoot` would resolve relative to it. It's an unusual layout for this project.

CHECK_OUTPUT: `$ tsc --noEmit` (no errors). `bun test tests/doctor.test.ts`: 20 pass, 0 fail, 27 expect() calls (same result in the live worktree and in the archive of 18b5a15).

FINDINGS:
- (blocking) (confirmed) src/doctor.ts:405–410 (`doctor()`: `listTickets(root, …)` next to the new `primaryRoot`)
  - Defect: finding #3 is only half-fixed. `worktreeRoot` is now resolved against the primary checkout, but ticket statuses are still read from `root`, which is the worktree's own branch. Since PR #77, status changes are committed straight to main after the branch is cut, so a worktree's copy of the tickets is stale.
  - Failure scenario: before this PR, doctor run from a worktree resolved `worktrees/0046/../worktrees` to a directory that doesn't exist, so it silently reported nothing. Now it resolves correctly, compares against stale ticket statuses, and warns that every live worktree is stale with "remove it". An agent can reasonably follow that advice and delete in-flight work.
  - How confirmed:
    - Real repo: I ran the 18b5a15 CLI from `/Users/woueziou/works/personal_projects/worktrees/0046`. It printed `worktree at …/worktrees/0046 has no matching inProgress ticket (number 0046) — stale, remove it`, and the same for 0052, 0054 and 0055. On the branch, ticket 0046 is `status: backlog`; on main it is `inProgress`.
    - Same binary from `/Users/woueziou/works/personal_projects/liteCodeAgent`: "No orphaned work found".
    - Scratch repo: ticket `planned` when the branch is cut, then `inProgress` committed on main. Doctor from main gives []; doctor from the worktree flags its own worktree.
    - The PR's test hides this by writing the ticket into the worktree itself (tests/doctor.test.ts, "doctor run from inside a ticket worktree…").
  - Same root cause, not probed separately:
    - `checkOrphanedInProgressTickets` also reads stale statuses from the worktree.
    - `checkPrimaryCheckoutLeak(root, …)` runs `git status` in the worktree rather than the primary checkout, so leaks into the primary checkout go undetected when doctor runs from a worktree. That one predates this PR.
- (blocking) (confirmed) src/doctor.ts:~262–275 (`checkStalePrStatus`, the `hasOpenPr` / `closed` logic)
  - Defect: when `gh` fails for some branches, an "unknown" lookup counts as "not open". The closed PR of an abandoned sibling branch then raises an **error**.
  - Failure scenario: ticket in `review`, `feat/attempt-one/0099` has PR CLOSED, and the `gh pr list` call for the live `feat/attempt-two/0099` fails (a 502, secondary rate limit or network blip; the calls now run in parallel through `Promise.all`). Output: `error 0099-x: status 'review' but its PR (…/pull/1) is closed — update the ticket`, plus a warn that the live branch is unverified. This is exactly the false positive finding #1 was meant to remove, and it exits 1. It contradicts the module's rule that a `gh` failure degrades to a warn, never a false verdict.
  - How confirmed: probe test with a fake `gh` returning CLOSED for attempt-one and `exit 1` for everything else.
- (non-blocking) (confirmed) src/doctor.ts:~268 (`lookups.find(...)`)
  - Defect: when no PR is open and the ticket's branches include both a MERGED and a CLOSED PR, the message reports whichever branch sorts first in `for-each-ref`, not the merged one.
  - Failure scenario: branches `feat/a-first/0099` (CLOSED) and `feat/b-second/0099` (MERGED). Output says "…/pull/1 is closed". The work actually landed, so the right fix is to mark the ticket done, not to reopen or abandon it.
  - Why narrow: it's still an error either way, so nothing is silently missed; only the suggested remediation points the wrong way.
  - How confirmed: probe test with a fake `gh`.
- Holds up (tried and couldn't break):
  - PR cache key (`repo\0branch`): one call per branch across both checks, no collision between repo and branch names. Caching the promise also dedupes the parallel `Promise.all` lookups, and within a single run it's fine that an "unknown" result is cached too.
  - Prunable handling: the orphaned-inProgress check doesn't count a prunable worktree as present, a surviving branch still suppresses the "abandoned" finding, and `checkOrphanedWorktrees` skips it.
  - `primaryCheckoutRoot` fallback: if `git worktree list` fails it returns [] and falls back to `root`, the same as before the PR.
  - Removing the `remoteBranchExists` gate: a local-only branch whose `gh` lookup returns "missing" gives no false finding.

REENTRY:
- Finding 1 (stale ticket statuses when run from a worktree): same-PR fixup, Priority high. Read tickets from `primaryRoot` (`listTickets(primaryRoot, …)`) for all ticket-driven checks, and point `checkPrimaryCheckoutLeak` at `primaryRoot`. Change the test so the ticket is committed on main after the branch is cut, instead of being written into the worktree.
- Finding 2 (gh failure turning into a "closed" error): same-PR fixup, Priority high. When any lookup is `unknown` and none is OPEN, don't raise the closed/merged error; keep only the "unverified" warn. Add a regression test for mixed CLOSED + failed lookups.
- Finding 3 (MERGED vs CLOSED message): same-PR fixup (one line: prefer a MERGED lookup over a CLOSED one). A new ticket via triage is also fine, since nothing is silently missed.
- The bare-repo layout that wasn't probed: none needed unless the project supports bare-repo setups.
